judgments.reasoning_cat1: "deemed properly given when delivered ... or sent by certified or registered mail" mixes a delivery rule with a dispatch rule, leaving the effective date of mailed notice uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Only Ajuba International's Michigan address is given for "the Company" although Ajuba India is a contracting party and the payer under 2.2 and 8.4, and no address is filled in for notices to the Board separately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence withholding clause with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates only "federal, state and local" (US) taxes although compensation is paid by Ajuba India to an employee required by 8.2(d) to reside in India, a fit question rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the ongoing provisions of this Agreement" is undefined and unenumerated — nothing tells the reader which provisions are ongoing, and "in accordance with their terms" begs the question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether Articles III, IV and V survive termination must be pieced together from 1.14, 3.2, 4.2 and Exhibit A ¶5 rather than from this clause, and post-term enforceability of the covenants would turn on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out for "that certain Non-Competition Agreement of even date herewith" leaves an unnamed second restrictive covenant in force alongside Article V without saying which governs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V already imposes non-competition duties, and 6.1(iii) has the Employee represent he is subject to no non-compete except as disclosed, so the relationship among these three provisions is genuinely open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Parties" is capitalised but never defined in this Agreement (only in Exhibit A), and the clause both denies and confers third-party rights in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent (MiraMed) is given rights throughout — 1.5, 1.7, V(b) and 8.4(b) — so third-party beneficiary status has real operative consequences that must be squared with 9.4's binding-on-successors language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional Michigan choice-of-law clause; "laws and decisions" is unusual phrasing but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Employment is performed in India by an Indian entity, and Exhibit A ¶17 chooses Michigan law in different terms, but nothing contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature pages are duplicated and partly unsigned, which counterparts language accommodates rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated forms of alienation end without a catch-all, and "Except as may be contrary to applicable law" is an open qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4 makes the Agreement binding on heirs and personal representatives and 8.3 contemplates payments to the Employee's estate, a mild tension with a blanket anti-alienation rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "disparage" is undefined and the obligation runs "During the Employment Term and thereafter" without limit, with no carve-out for testimony or legally required statements; the sentence also ends without a period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶3 states a differently scoped non-disparagement duty limited to "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" and with a legal-requirement exception, so the two instruments pull apart on the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow recusal promise with a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the Employee may sit on the Board, which 8.4(b) also assumes; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "may be brought against any of parties" is both permissive and grammatically defective, so whether the clause is a mandatory forum selection or a mere consent to jurisdiction is genuinely arguable — exactly the permissive/mandatory issue courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 9.10's Michigan choice of law and with an employee residing in India under 8.2(d), the clause's mandatory character is the pivot for any forum challenge, but no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain unfilled blanks for the Employment Agreement date and termination date, garbled text ("at band separation from Comnipany"), and a mis-lettered paragraph run.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital D's desire to release "any and all claims" points more broadly than operative ¶1, which expressly excludes claims to compel payment of amounts due under the Employment Agreement — a recital/operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of statutes closed by "any other claims ... in any local, state or federal or other forum" raises a general-versus-specific reach question, and the carve-out "excluding only those to compel the payment of amounts due" is narrow and contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The release is the condition of severance under 8.4, so its scope must be reconciled with 8.4's continuing payment obligation and with Exhibit A ¶5's preserved covenants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all other assets, materials and information of any kind or nature, belonging or pertaining to Company" is an unlimited catch-all following an enumerated list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.2 and 4.2 already impose return obligations in narrower defined terms (Confidential Information, Company Technology), so three overlapping return duties with different scopes coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "For so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" makes the whole duty conditional on an instrument this contract never mentions, and "the circumstances of Employee's resignation" assumes a resignation even where the Company terminated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be reconciled with 9.13, which imposes a mutual, unconditional non-disparagement duty during and after the Employment Term; the RSU condition has no referent anywhere in the Agreement or Schedules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To never seek or accept employment with Company" is a sentence fragment with no subject or operative verb, and the perpetual bar plus waiver of "any claim" is drastically one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Article VIII or elsewhere contemplates a permanent no-rehire bar, but no provision directly contradicts it either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short acknowledgment that the confidentiality, proprietary-rights and non-compete duties continue; the terms are identified by subject-matter rather than section number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 9.7's survival clause and Articles III, IV and V, and helps resolve the vagueness of "ongoing provisions"; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a reasonable amount of the Employee's time" and "reasonable notice" are soft but conventional cooperation standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The promise to reimburse lost wages sits alongside 8.4's severance without any coordination, a small gap rather than an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A factual acknowledgment with a clear cross-reference to paragraph 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the release in ¶1; nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acknowledgment that the Employee "was advised to consult with an attorney and did so" states a fact that may be untrue, but its wording is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital C says only that he was given the opportunity to consult counsel, while this operative paragraph asserts he actually did — a small recital/operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 21-day consideration period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the ¶10 revocation period and the ADEA release in ¶1; no internal inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The addresses for delivering a revocation are left blank, so the mechanics of the very right the paragraph creates cannot be performed as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "This Agreement is not effective until this revocation period has expired" must be squared with ¶11, which additionally conditions the Company's obligations on written confirmation of non-revocation, and with 8.4's requirement of execution "without revocation".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading speaks of severance payments but the text says "the Company's obligations" generally, leaving unclear which obligations are conditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 conditions severance only on execution without revocation, not on written confirmation, so this paragraph adds a condition the Employment Agreement does not impose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional voluntariness and no-reliance acknowledgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶15's entire-agreement clause; nothing contrary located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "legitimate business purposes" is an undefined and elastic exception to the Company's confidentiality promise, sitting against a tightly limited exception for the Employee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats verbatim the same undefined standard used in 3.3 of the Employment Agreement, so the vagueness is duplicated rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard non-admission clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with recital D's "without any admission of liability".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "regarding the matters set forth herein" is a self-referential limit that makes the integration clause's reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 5 expressly preserves Employment Agreement obligations and 9.8 of the Agreement preserves a separate Non-Competition Agreement, so the integration promise must be read subject to at least two other instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional Section 1542-style acknowledgment of unknown facts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces ¶1's release of known and unknown claims; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted Michigan choice-of-law clause excluding renvoi.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantially matches 9.10 of the Agreement; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard reformation-or-excision severability with clear alternatives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.2 of the Agreement provides plain severance without reformation, a different salvage rule for the two documents but not an operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It releases the Company from obligations "under the Severance Agreement", a term that appears nowhere and matches no document in the instrument, and the sentence ends in a comma without completion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The severance obligation actually lives in Section 8.4 of the Employment Agreement, and this forfeiture provision cannot be reconciled with 8.4's unconditional payment promise once the Release is signed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "other strategic partnership arrangements" is a general catch-all closing a specific list, and "providing recommendations" is an advisory duty of uncertain content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 2.1 duties are the benchmark for 8.4(a)'s "material diminution" Good Reason test and are subject to 2.1's deemed-amendment mechanic, so their scope carries real consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "including Ajuba US and all subsidiaries" attached to Finance/Accounting/Cash Management is ambiguous as to how far beyond Ajuba India the responsibility runs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) says consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of cash management, accounting and sales and marketing is not a material diminution, and 2.1 deems this Schedule amended in that event — so this duty and the Good Reason carve-out sit in direct tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear statement of reporting lines qualified only by "directly or indirectly".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a Schedule 2.1 duty and therefore part of the 8.4(a) diminution benchmark, and 2.1 gives Schedule 2.1 priority over the Bylaws, which may allocate authority differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-word reporting line with no ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 says the Employee "shall report directly to the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)", while this line says he reports to the Chairman — and 2.1 makes Schedule 2.1 control in a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete attendance obligation with a stated cadence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.1 and 9.14's recusal duty; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Employee shall oversee closing down the Ajuba UK operations" is a duty of effort, yet completion is defined by named individuals' final employment dates and a third-party lease termination the Employee cannot control.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) pays the Reorganization Bonus on the twelve-month anniversary "if the foregoing actions have been completed", so this completion test can fall after the payment date with no rule for that case.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is "Restructure" while the duty is merely to oversee termination of a lease and the completion test is the lease's termination, so "restructured" carries an uncertain meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) conditions $200,000 on the Novi office being "restructured ... in accordance with Schedule I", making this loose completion test the payment trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclaimer resting on "good faith estimates" and referring to "Contemplated Transactions" defined in an undated Stock Purchase Agreement ("June __, 2005") not otherwise part of this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) describes Schedule I as setting forth "the specific cost savings for each action and a reasonable risk assessment", which this paragraph then disclaims — the operative clause and the Schedule point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cost-allocation sentence; "associated with" is slightly open but the allocation is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ajuba is made solely responsible for the costs while 2.2(f) makes Ajuba India the payer of the Reorganization Bonus, a minor allocation mismatch between affiliated obligors.
